title: Washington withholds $2.87 billion over California’s in-home care claims

beats.text: May 13, 2026. A letter from the federal Medicaid agency to California.
Then July. Then October. Three letters, each withholding money.
On in-home care alone: 2.87 billion dollars.

visual.label: withheld on in-home care claims, federal share

beats.text: These are official letters. A deferral withholds money while documents are checked.

visual.text: A deferral withholds money while documents are checked. It is not a verdict.

beats.text: It isn’t a verdict.

visual.text: A deferral withholds money while documents are checked. It is not a verdict.

beats.text: In-Home Supportive Services pays caregivers, often family members, to help elderly and disabled people stay home.
Counties run it, the State pays, and Washington pays a share.
Quarter by quarter: 1.13 billion dollars.

visual.label: Withheld on personal care, by quarter

beats.text: Then 646.4 million. Then 1.09 billion.

visual.label: Withheld on personal care, by quarter

beats.text: Part is the agency’s own estimate, for growth faster than the average of other states.

visual.line: Part is an estimate from growth faster than the average of all other states; part is claims that failed specific tests.

beats.text: Part comes from tests on the State’s claims.

visual.line: Part is an estimate from growth faster than the average of all other states; part is claims that failed specific tests.

beats.text: All told, the three letters withheld 3.47 billion dollars. Personal care is most of it.

visual.label: withheld from California in the three letters, federal share

beats.text: More than all the immigration-status items that drew attention before: 43.4 million.
In July, a federal health department notice put that quarter’s whole deferral at about 867.5 million.
Who covers the gap? A deferral is repaid from the State’s General Fund until released.

visual.text: A deferral is repaid from the State’s General Fund until released.

beats.text: For other deferrals, the State budgeted 100 million dollars, then raised it to 200 million.
For the 2.87 billion on personal care? Neither estimate has a line.
